source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of exact tab-separated Greek payload, retaining whitespace and variant markers.

notes: The opening accumulates what was heard, seen and touched before returning to the act of announcement in verse 3. “Word of life” is not expanded into an explicit identification.
The pinned text reads “our joy”; other witnesses read “your joy.”
vocabulary: Righteous or just; the same word family recurs throughout the letter.

notes: “Love of God” and “love of the Father” can refer to love from God or love for God.
The source distinguishes “I write” and “I have written.” Its verse 14 begins with the address to children; some English numbering places that address at the end of verse 13.
The final Greek clause uses not and all together; “none of them belonged to us” takes the negation as applying to each of those who left.
The pinned reading is “all of you know”; another reading is “you know all things.”
vocabulary: An atoning means or sacrifice; the term has been rendered expiation or propitiation.
Life, livelihood or possessions; here the boast concerns the resources of worldly life.
Anointing. The image is retained without replacing it with an explanatory noun.

notes: “When he is revealed” can also be understood as “when it is revealed,” referring to what the children of God will be.
The Greek statements about not sinning are categorical. The present-tense forms have also been understood as habitual practice; this is not added to the text. Compare 1:8–2:2.
The syntax can connect the assurance to God being greater than the condemning heart; the relation of divine knowledge to assurance and judgment remains compressed.
vocabulary: The inward parts, used for compassion.

notes: The pinned text reads simply “does not confess Jesus”; some witnesses repeat or expand the embodied confession of verse 2.
The pinned text says “we love,” without an expressed object. Other witnesses add “him” or “God.”
vocabulary: Only or unique, here describing the Son.
Atoning sacrifice; the same term appears in 2:2.
Punishment, the stated connection to fear in this passage.

notes: Water and blood are not defined here. Readings connect them with Jesus’ baptism and death, sacramental imagery or the affirmation of his embodied life and death.
The pinned Greek has the Spirit, water and blood as the three witnesses. It does not contain the expanded heavenly witnesses known as the Comma Johanneum.
“Sin that leads to death” is not specified. The subject of “will give” is implicit; the Greek can connect the giving with the one petitioned or with the one making the request.
The pinned text has “keeps him,” not “keeps himself.” The protecting “one born of God” can be understood as the Son; the wording is retained without replacing it with a name.
“This” may refer to Jesus Christ or point back to the true one. The pronoun is not replaced with an interpretive noun.
vocabulary: Beget or give birth. The verse uses masculine language for the one who begets.
Literally “toward death,” rendered leading to death.

2.reason: Pinned 1 John 2:14 includes the children address placed at the end of TSW 2:13. Label-level comparators remain unchanged; compare 2:13–14 together.
